description: An un-narrowed `find` with a delete action is the recursive force-delete of its root spelled through an enumerator, and from the repo root no tier saw it until 2026-09-15 (DEF-815): the zone check judges an un-narrowed root by what it encloses and the repo root answers False by design (lane 2's shortcut, so that `find . -name '*.pyc' -delete` stays an everyday command), the catastrophic classifier was reached only from the rm-shaped arms, and the speed bump had no find predicate -- so `find . -delete`, the rootless `find -delete` (GNU's default root), `find . -exec rm -rf {} +` and `find . -type f -delete` all ALLOWED from the checkout while `rm -rf .` was refused with the catastrophic text (driven at HEAD on a throwaway carrying the hook tree). Fix: `_bash_patterns.has_catastrophic_find_delete` hands every root of an un-narrowed find with a delete action to the rm arm's own classifier through the rm arm's own directory chain, `write_guard._bash_dangerous_reason` refuses on it with `_denial_reasons.CATASTROPHIC_FIND_DELETE` ahead of the maintenance gate, and `_speedbump._pred_rmrf` gained the find arm for an un-narrowed root that is not catastrophic and not roster-ephemeral (one nudge, as for the rm spelling). NARROWED means a name-or-path predicate in force BEFORE the action (`_find_is_narrowed`): the lane's first cut kept `-type` and the attribute tests (`-size`, `-perm`, `-mtime`, `-user`, `-links`) as narrowing and read a predicate anywhere in the span, and both reviews drove the one-token exits -- `find / -size +0c -delete`, `find . -delete -name zzz`, `find . ! -name zzz -delete`, `find / -name zzz -o -delete`, and the verb spellings the rm arm admits (`FIND`, `-exec /bin/rm`, `-exec env rm`). The attempts below vary along ROOT SPELLING, ACTION SPELLING and PREDICATE PLACEMENT, because a corpus flat along any of those axes would have reported the wall on one spelling and missed the rest.
